title: Vienna Convention on Consular Relations (1963) Article 36 Violation — Failure of Consular Notification During De Facto Detention at Santiago Airport
category: International Aviation / Human Rights / Treaty Law

incident.location: Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport, Santiago, Chile

allegation_summary: During the LA8159 incident at Santiago Airport on July 5, 2024, the passenger — an Italian citizen (with Brazilian birth nationality) — was held by PDI and airport security in the jetbridge and terminal areas for an extended period without being informed of his right to contact Italian or Brazilian consular authorities. Despite being a foreign national facing a de facto deprivation of liberty (prevented from boarding his flight, held in a confined area, subjected to security procedures based on a false accusation), Chilean authorities failed to provide the consular notification required under Article 36 of the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations (VCCR), to which Chile, Brazil, and Italy are all parties. The passenger was not informed of his right to consular access, his consulates were not notified of his detention, and any communication to consular authorities was not facilitated.
